name: 2CRSi

profile.address: 7019, Lake Street, Brainardsville, Village of Chateaugay, Town of Chateaugay, Town of Bellmont, Franklin County, New York, 12920
profile.reading:
This Franklin County, New York site sits at 7019 NY Route 374 (locally mapped as Lake Street) in the hamlet of Brainardsville, part of the Town of Chateaugay, roughly midway between Malone and the Canadian border. The property is the former Church Energy Center, a wood-fired biomass power plant, and it is now the subject of a data center development involving three named parties: PPS Services Group, a Kansas City, Missouri firm led by president Lou Gonzales; Architecture, Engineering, and Land Surveying Northeast (AES), a Plattsburgh engineering firm; and 2CRSi, the France-based manufacturer of high-performance and AI computing servers that is listed as this facility's operator.

According to reporting on a March 2026 presentation to the Chateaugay Town Board, the plan calls for a data center reaching 40 megawatts at full build-out, developed in phases. Phase one pairs roughly 300 to 400 acres of solar photovoltaic capacity (about 10 MW) with battery storage, under a 25-year power purchase agreement priced at $50 per megawatt-hour; phase two would restart the site's dormant biomass generator to cover the balance of the load. A wetland delineation, visual assessment, and decommissioning plan were still due as of the project's environmental review, which local reporting described as substantially complete by June 2026. Initial staffing was projected at two to three workers, with potential growth toward 25 or more as the facility matures, and permitting was described as moving relatively quickly toward approval.

This is a second, distinct New York project for 2CRSi, which separately established a manufacturing, sales, and hosting campus on an 80-acre former Pfizer property in Rouses Point, about 20 miles north in Clinton County, beginning in 2021 with a combined initial investment of roughly $12 million from 2CRSi and its real estate partner, ERS Investors.

No first-party page on 2CRSi's own website describes the Chateaugay building specifically, and no IT capacity, white-space square footage, tenancy, or redundancy figures for the completed data center have been published. That absence is worth noting alongside a separate fact: in June 2026, the short-seller Grizzly Research published a report alleging that 2CRSi's US subsidiary fabricated revenue and projections through undisclosed related-party transactions. 2CRSi has publicly and directly disputed those allegations point by point. Given that unresolved dispute, readers should treat any claims about this project's operational status or scale as provisional until the facility itself, rather than press coverage of its permitting, is independently confirmed.

reading:
2CRSi is a French technology group founded in 2005 and headquartered in Strasbourg, listed on Euronext Growth Paris under the ticker AL2SI with ISIN FR0013341781. Its core business is designing and building energy efficient servers for artificial intelligence, high performance computing and cloud workloads, which is what makes its presence in a data center registry unusual. It is a hardware manufacturer that has become entangled in United States site development, and the registry lists it as operator of a New York site rather than as a colocation landlord.

The facility recorded here is at 7019 State Route 374 in Brainardsville, in the Town of Chateaugay, Franklin County, New York, roughly midway between Malone and the Canadian border. The property is the former Church Energy Center, a wood chip fired biomass power plant that shut down about a decade ago when it could not meet its contractual power obligations. The best account of what is planned there is not corporate but municipal. Reporting on a March 2026 presentation to the Chateaugay Town Board describes a partnership of AES, a Plattsburgh architecture, engineering and land surveying firm, PPS Services Group of Kansas City, and 2CRSi, working with landowners named as Bub Earl and Joe Church. The plan targets 40 megawatts at full build out. Phase one is a solar photovoltaic array of roughly 10 megawatts spread across about 300 to 400 acres, paired with battery storage discussed in the range of 180 to 360 megawatt hours, under a twenty five year power purchase agreement priced at 50 dollars per megawatt hour. A later phase would repower the biomass generator to cover the balance of the load. The town board placed 10,000 dollars in escrow to pay for engineering review of the plans and took the role of lead agency for coordinated permitting review, with wetland delineation and jurisdictional determination among the studies still to come.

The 40 megawatt, 10 megawatt and battery figures are three different things: a target site load, planned on site generation and planned storage. None is a measured IT load. 2CRSi's own regulated disclosure adds a much smaller number. In its detailed point by point response to a Grizzly Research short seller report of June 18, 2026, the company stated that the Chateaugay property is owned by its customer Dr. Joseph Church and that the site includes a 2 megawatt data center, and that the Rouses Point building where it runs production is owned by ERS Investors rather than by 2CRSi. Grizzly alleged fabricated revenue booked through undisclosed related parties. 2CRSi disputed the allegations, said NewYork GreenCloud is a customer in which neither the company nor its founder holds equity, and said it was considering action. That dispute is unresolved, and this registry records it as a dispute rather than adopting either side's account.
